The Gross Floor Area (GFA) is the total square footage of buildings on the property, measured as the area between the outside exterior walls of the building(s). This includes all areas inside the building(s), including supporting areas, but excludes parking. GFA is not the same as rentable space. This data is reported through Energy Star Portfolio Manager.
The total area of a parking structure that is completely enclosed on all four sides and has a roof.

field: BERDO Emissions Gross Floor Area (Sq Ft)
definition: The Gross Floor Area used for BERDO emissions calculations is the sum of all reported gross floor area plus any reported enclosed parking area. This value represents the total square footage used as the basis for calculating a building’s emissions under BERDO.
The largest property type indicates the single, primary use of the building reported through Energy Star Portfolio Manager.

field: All Property Types With Gross Floor Area (Sq Ft)
definition: All property types reported through Energy Star Portfolio Manager, including the Gross Floor Area (GFA) associated with each type.

Site Energy Use Intensity is the annual amount of all the energy a building consumes onsite divided by the Gross Floor Area. This metric is an effective means to compare the energy efficiency between two buildings. The lower the EUI the more efficient the building.

The ENERGY STAR Score shows how efficiently a building uses energy compared to similar buildings nationwide, with adjustments for size, location, and operating conditions. Scores range from 1 to 100, where 50 represents the national median and 75 or higher indicates top performance that may qualify for ENERGY STAR certification. Only certain property types are eligible to receive a score: data centers, hospitals, hotels, K–12 schools, medical offices, multifamily housing, offices, parking facilities, residence halls and dormitories, retail stores, senior care communities, supermarkets and grocery stores, swimming pools, warehouses, wastewater treatment plants, and worship facilities. Because the scoring system is updated as national data and methods improve, a building’s score may change over time even if its energy use stays the same.
Total Site Energy is the annual amount of all the energy a building(s) consumes onsite. Total Site Energy is measured in Thousands of British Thermal Units.
Natural Gas Usage is the total annual amount of gas a building consumes onsite. Natural Gas Usage is measured in Thousands of British Thermal Units.
Natural Gas Emissions is the total amount of greenhouse gas emissions associated with the building's Natural Gas Usage. Emissions are measured in Kilograms of Carbon Dioxide Equivalent.
Electricity Usage is the total annual amount of electricity a building consumes onsite. This includes Renewable System Electricity Usage. Electricity Usage is measured in kilowatt-hours.
Electricity Emissions is the total amount of greenhouse gas emissions associated with the building's Electricity Usage. Emissions are measured in Kilograms of Carbon Dioxide Equivalent.
Renewable System Electricity Usage Onsite is the total annual amount of electricity produced from onsite solar panels or wind turbines that a building consumes onsite.
District Hot Water Usage is the total annual amount of energy a building consumes onsite from district hot water systems. District Hot Water Usage is measured in Thousands of British Thermal Units.
District Hot Water Emissions is the total amount of greenhouse gas emissions associated with the building's District Hot Water Usage. Emissions are measured in Kilograms of Carbon Dioxide Equivalent.

District Chilled Water Usage is the total annual amount of energy a building consumes onsite from district chilled water systems. District Chilled Water Usage is measured in Thousands of British Thermal Units.

District Chilled Water Emissions is the total amount of greenhouse gas emissions associated with the building's District Chilled Water Usage. Emissions are measured in Kilograms of Carbon Dioxide Equivalent.

Water Usage Intensity is the annual water source consumption divided by the building Gross Area.

Total Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions are calculated by adding the annual greenhouse gas emissions from all fuels and electricity consumption for a building. Emissions for each fuel are calculated by multiplying the annual site energy for each fuel by the default emissions factor for that specific fuel type. Emissions are reported in kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e). This is an estimated value as default emissions factors for fuels and the electric grid are applied. The emissions factor used for electricity is the 2024 projected value as reported in the BERDO Policies and Procedures. All other emissions factors used in this calculation are from Energy Star Portfolio Manager. The actual Total GHG Emissions value for BERDO compliance will depend on any custom emissions factors applied and the portion of electricity generated from renewable sources. For more information about the default emissions factors and future applications for custom emissions factors please see the BERDO Regulations & Policy documents.

Compliance Status is the status of a building's compliance with BERDO reporting and verification requirements. 
  - In Compliance: Data has been reported, accepted by a third-party verifier if required, and accepted by the BERDO Team.
  - Pending Revisions: Data has been reported and accepted by the third-party verifier if required, but acceptance by the BERDO Team is pending further corrections or clarification of submitted data.
  - Not Submitted: Data has not been submitted to the BERDO Team.

First Emissions Compliance Year (Projected) is the first data year that the building is expected to have to comply with an emissions standard. Commercial buildings on a tax parcel with a Gross Floor Area of 35,000 sq ft or more as well as residential buildings on a tax parcel with 35 or more residential units will have to comply in reporting year 2026 based on 2025 data. All other buildings on the Covered Buildings List will have to comply in reporting year 2031 based on 2030 data.

A Corresponding Campus ID is displayed if a building has been reported through Energy Star Portfolio Manager as part of a campus. A campus is a collection of two or more buildings that function as a single property. They are generally owned and operated by the same party and typically have shared energy systems. If a building has been reported as part of a campus, the row of data displayed for the building may not reflect the full energy and water usage of the entire building. To view the reported energy usage for the full campus, refer to the building's corresponding Campus ID in the Data Disclosure – Campuses tab.
